title: Garden and Orchard
premise: Oscar Eriksen's inherited vineyard is drowning in debt, and he has trained himself to treat love as a liability he cannot afford. When a snowstorm strands his old rival, Ingrid Voss, and her estranged business partner — the woman Oscar loved and lost a decade ago, Maren Kowalczyk — at his farmhouse, three histories collide over one long winter night. As the thaw comes, Oscar must choose between selling the orchard to save it and keeping the one person who makes staying feel like home; he chooses truth over duty, confesses both love and insolvency, and finds that Maren stays anyway, buying the vineyard together with him as partners in every sense.
about_author: August Ishikawa is the pen name of a former sommelier who spent six years working harvests across northern Europe before turning to fiction. They write quiet, weather-driven romances about people who mistake practicality for peace.

chapters.title: The Last Train Schedule
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. He audits the vineyard's debts on the eve of the auction deadline, cataloguing what can be sold: cellar stock, the south slope, eventually the house itself. A letter from the bank arrives. The emotional beat is controlled dread — Oscar rehearsing the arithmetic of loss as fluently as he once rehearsed tenderness.

chapters.title: Two Tickets, One Storm
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She arrives in the valley to finalize buying the neighboring estate, carrying an unsigned partnership contract with Ingrid Voss, her former lover turned rival bidder. The snow begins early. The emotional beat is ambivalence — Maren telling herself this trip is business while rereading a ten-year-old postcard from Oscar.

chapters.title: Stranded at Eriksen Farm
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The roads close; Ingrid's car slides into his ditch with Maren inside. He takes in the two women who represent everything he lost and everything he could lose next. The beat is reluctant hospitality — wine opened out of obligation, tension crackling under politeness.

chapters.title: What the Cellar Remembers
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. While Ingrid sleeps, Maren wanders the cellar and finds the barrel they carved their initials into the summer they were twenty-three. Oscar finds her there. Old wounds surface: why she left for Lyon, why he never wrote. The beat is aching intimacy interrupted by dawn.

chapters.title: Ingrid's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ingrid's POV. She wakes first and reads the situation instantly, then reveals she knows Oscar's vineyard is failing — she intends to buy it at auction herself. But she offers Maren a choice: sign the partnership or walk away. The beat is cold clarity; loyalty revealed as leverage.

chapters.title: Pruning Season
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Snowbound days stretch into work: the three of them pruning dead vines side by side. Oscar teaches Maren the grafts her father invented; laughter returns like a trespasser. The beat is warmth against will — Oscar catching himself hoping, then punishing the hope.

chapters.title: The Heart Is a Muscle
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren confronts Oscar: he trains his heart like a laborer trains a back, and it's breaking him. She asks him to fight for the vineyard — and for her — instead of surrendering gracefully to Ingrid's offer. The beat is confrontation as confession, ending with a kiss neither retreats from.

chapters.title: Auction Day
chapters.summary: Ingrid's POV. The thaw opens the roads; at the auction, Ingrid bids against a faceless developer, forcing Oscar to decide whether to let go. In a twist, Ingrid withdraws — not from mercy, but because Maren signed nothing and Ingrid refuses to win by default. The beat is bitter triumph and unexpected grace.

chapters.title: Truth Over Duty
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar publicly discloses the full debt and asks Maren not to rescue him but to build with him: co-ownership, shared risk, no more containment. Ingrid, wounded but honest, signs her own contract elsewhere. The beat is vulnerability as strength — the last train leaves without anyone on it.

chapters.title: First Bud
chapters.summary: Maren's POV, epilogue in spring. The two estates merge under one name; the initials-carved barrel becomes the tasting room's centerpiece. Ingrid sends a case of congratulatory wine with a note that says only 'You were right.' The beat is earned peace — love that stayed after every train left.
